title: The bear who was an official soldier in World War Two
hook: A brown bear was an official soldier in the Polish army.
summary: Polish soldiers adopted a bear cub in Iran, then enlisted him with a rank so he could board a ship to Italy, where he carried ammunition crates at Monte Cassino.
sources: Wikipedia: Wojtek (bear): found in Iran 1942, enlisted as a private in the 22nd Artillery Supply Company to travel by ship to Italy in 1944, carried ammunition at Monte Cassino, lived at Edinburgh Zoo until 1963.
Imperial War Museum and Polish Institute and Sikorski Museum accounts of Wojtek and the Polish II Corps.

lines.text: A brown bear was an official soldier in the Polish army.
Soldiers found him as a cub in Iran in nineteen forty-two.
But in nineteen forty-four, the ship to Italy banned animals.
So they gave him a rank, and a name in the records.
Private Wojtek sailed with them to the war.
At Monte Cassino, he carried crates of shells, and never dropped one.
lines.caps: At *Monte Cassino, | he carried *crates, | never *dropped one

lines.text: After the war, he lived in Edinburgh Zoo, visited by old comrades.
The bear who earned his place on the army's books.

post.caption:
The army needed a paper trick to take a bear to war, and it worked.
Would you have signed him up too?
